stories.headline: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island; Iran fires ballistic missiles at US bases in Jordan

key_facts.fact: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30 after the IRGC was observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the waterway.
key_facts.excerpt: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) was observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the vital waterway, a US official confirmed to RFE/RL.

key_facts.fact: The August 30 strikes were the first publicly reported direct US attack on Iranian military positions in more than a month; the previous one was July 29.
key_facts.excerpt: The August 30 strikes mark the first publicly reported direct US attack on Iranian military positions in more than a month and come as Washington seeks to restore shipping through one of the world's most strategically important maritime chokepoints.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said it retaliated by firing ballistic missiles at the King Hussein and Al-Azraq air bases in Jordan; Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles that entered its airspace early on August 31.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC later said it fired ballistic missiles at two bases housing US forces in Jordan in retaliation. Jordan, a close US ally, said it intercepted eight incoming missiles that entered its airspace early on August 31.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices rose after the strikes, with Brent crude climbing above $90 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate above $85.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices rose after news of the latest US strikes, with Brent crude climbing above $90 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate rising above $85.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said that as of August 30 its blockade of Iran had redirected 83 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command said its forces were continuing to enforce a blockade against Iran and, as of Aug. 30, had redirected 83 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two.

key_facts.fact: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is among the lowest of the conflict, at about five vessels a day in either direction and some days none at all, according to maritime-security firm Auxilium Worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: Ralby said traffic is among the lowest seen during the conflict, with about five vessels a day traveling in either direction and some days with no traffic at all.

stories.headline: Kyiv depot strike toll hits 38 as Moscow says it is preparing mass strikes on Ukraine's power grid

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said on Sunday, August 30 that the death toll from the Russian strike on an ammunition warehouse in Myla, west of Kyiv, rose to 38, with four people still missing and at least 52 injured — the war's deadliest attack this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The death toll from a Russian strike on a warehouse west of Kyiv, the war's deadliest attack this year, rose to 38 with four people still missing, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday. … At least 52 people were injured, said Tymur Tkachenko.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defence Ministry said on August 30 it had begun preparing 'massive strikes' on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, framing it as retaliation for Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian retailers Wildberries and Ozon and on its oil and gas sector.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Russian Armed Forces have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure in response to what Moscow describes as ongoing attacks by the Kyiv regime on Russia's civilian infrastructure and fuel and energy facilities," the defence ministry in Moscow said on Telegram.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called large-scale strikes on Ukraine's energy sector 'an appropriate response' to what he described as Kyiv's targeting of Russia's civilian economy.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said large-scale strikes against Ukraine's energy sector would be "an appropriate response" to what he called Ukraine's "path of escalation" and targeting of Russia's civilian economy.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces downed or neutralized almost 500 Ukrainian drones overnight, while drone strikes set fire to the Kirishi refinery, one of Russia's largest and the only one in the country's northwest.
key_facts.excerpt: Also on Sunday, Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces downed or neutralized almost 500 Ukrainian drones launched overnight. … the drone strikes set fire to a major oil refinery in Kirishi, southeast of St. Petersburg.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said Russian forces launched nearly 1,500 drones over four days, including roughly 800 jet-powered Shahed variants, which he called the military's 'most difficult task' to intercept.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the Ukrainian president, Russian forces launched nearly 1,500 drones over a four-day period, including roughly 800 jet-powered Shahed variants. He described intercepting the faster, jet-powered models as the military's "most difficult task".

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's new defence minister Yevhen Khmara said in his first briefing, released Sunday, that he inherited a $27 billion funding gap and is considering bringing forward part of a €90 billion ($104 billion) European loan planned for next year.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's new Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara said the ministry has options for closing the $27 billion funding gap he inherited from his predecessor … The ministry is considering bringing forward part of a 90 billion euro ($104 billion) European loan planned for next year.

stories.headline: NASA's $4.3B Roman Space Telescope launches on Falcon Heavy toward L2

key_facts.fact: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Sunday, August 30, aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center.
key_facts.excerpt: The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT Sunday aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

key_facts.fact: The 9,200-kilogram spacecraft separated from the upper stage 31 minutes after liftoff; the two side boosters landed at Cape Canaveral while the center core was expended. It was the 13th Falcon Heavy launch since 2018.
key_facts.excerpt: The rocket's payload, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, deployed from the upper stage 31 minutes later. The rocket's two side boosters landed at separate pads at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, while the central booster was expended. This was the 13th launch of the Falcon Heavy, dating back to its debut in 2018.

key_facts.fact: Roman will spend about 100 days travelling to the Earth-Sun L2 point, 1.5 million kilometres away; the $4.3 billion mission has a five-year prime mission and propellant for at least 10 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Roman will spend the next 100 days traveling to the Earth-sun L-2 Lagrange point, 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. … The $4.3 billion Roman is NASA's latest flagship space telescope, with a five-year prime mission but enough propellant to operate in a halo orbit around the L-2 point for at least 10 years.

key_facts.fact: The telescope is expected to survey the sky about 1,000 times faster than Hubble, and NASA expects to release its first images in early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: There, it's expected to rapidly scan the sky and survey the universe about 1,000 times faster than the Hubble Space Telescope. … NASA said it expects to release its first images from the Roman Space Telescope in early 2027.

key_facts.fact: Roman launched nearly a year ahead of schedule and within budget, and is NASA's first space telescope named after a woman.
key_facts.excerpt: Launching nearly a year ahead of schedule and within budget, Roman is NASA's first space telescope to be named after a woman.

key_facts.fact: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called the launch 'exactly the kind of success story we want to see across NASA,' noting delivery ahead of schedule and on budget.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called the launch of the telescope "exactly the kind of success story we want to see across NASA."

stories.headline: Shein completes Hong Kong IPO, raising $1.7B at a $26B valuation — a quarter of its 2022 peak

key_facts.fact: Shein raised $1.7 billion in its Hong Kong IPO, giving it a market value of about $26 billion, far below the nearly $100 billion it commanded in 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: The fast-fashion retailer raised $1.7 billion in Hong Kong, giving it a market value of $26 billion that's a far cry from the $100 billion it once commanded.

key_facts.fact: The deal was priced at HK$48.56 a share, near the midpoint of the HK$47.60–HK$49.50 marketed range, raising about HK$13.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is set to price the deal at HK$48.56 a share, near the midpoint of its HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 range, the people said, raising about HK$13.6 billion ($1.73 billion).

key_facts.fact: The IPO values Shein at over 15 times forward earnings — roughly double the multiple of rival PDD Holdings, Temu's owner — with the stock set to debut on Tuesday, September 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Shein's long-awaited IPO valued the company at over 15 times forward earnings … That's about double the ratio commanded by its competitor Temu's PDD Holdings Inc. … threaten to weigh on the stock as it prepares to debut on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Cornerstone investors committed about $383 million, led by existing shareholders Boyu Capital, Tiger Global and General Atlantic, with Tencent, Greenwoods, Taikang Life and UBS Asset Management also participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Cornerstone investors have committed to buying about $383 million worth of shares, according to the company's prospectus. Existing shareholders Boyu Capital, Tiger Global and General Atlantic are leading the cornerstone participation, while Tencent, Greenwoods, Taikang Life and UBS Asset Management are also set to invest.

key_facts.fact: Shein expects first-half revenue growth to broadly track the 1.1% it reported in the first quarter, with operating margin declining slightly, and has agreed to pay up to $3.5 billion in cash to certain earlier private-round investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Shein expects first-half revenue growth to broadly track the 1.1% growth it reported in the first quarter, while its operating margin is expected to decline slightly. The company has also agreed to pay as much as $3.5 billion in cash to certain investors who purchased special shares during earlier private funding rounds.

stories.headline: FSB chair Bailey warns G20 of disorderly market correction as ministers meet in Asheville

key_facts.fact: In a letter submitted ahead of the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors meetings on 31 August and 1 September, FSB Chair Andrew Bailey warned that markets remain vulnerable to a potentially disorderly correction that could spread across borders.
key_facts.excerpt: This letter was submitted to G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) ahead of their meetings on 31 August and 1 September 2026. Against the backdrop of the ongoing Middle East conflict, FSB Chair, Andrew Bailey warns that markets remain vulnerable to a potentially disorderly correction that could spread across borders.

key_facts.fact: Bailey singled out fragilities in sovereign debt markets, vulnerabilities in private credit and stretched asset valuations, against the backdrop of the ongoing Middle East conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: particularly given fragilities in sovereign debt markets; vulnerabilities in private credit; as well as stretched asset valuations.

key_facts.fact: The letter warns that frontier AI models, with increasingly sophisticated autonomy and threat capabilities, may materially alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber risk and undermine market confidence system-wide.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter warns that frontier AI may have the ability materially to alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber risk, which could undermine market confidence system-wide.

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is hosting the G20 finance meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, pressing counterparts to shrink trade imbalances, boost growth and sever business ties to Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faces a major test of his economic diplomacy skills this week as he presses finance leaders from the G20 major economies to shrink global trade imbalances, boost growth and sever business ties to Iran, while trying to calm worries about rising U.S. debt and bond yields.

key_facts.fact: Total US public debt crossed $40 trillion on August 19, 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest levels in 19 years this month, and Bessent doubled scheduled buybacks of longer-dated Treasuries to $4 billion per operation.
key_facts.excerpt: Total U.S. public debt crossed the $40 trillion mark on August 19 after doubling since 2017 … Yields on 30-year debt reached their highest levels in 19 years this month, but Bessent surprised markets by announcing a doubling of scheduled buybacks of longer-dated Treasuries to $4 billion per operation.

stories.headline: Iceland narrowly votes against resuming EU accession talks in record-turnout referendum

key_facts.fact: Iceland voted against resuming EU accession talks, with 52.8% rejecting the government's proposal and 47.2% backing it out of more than 225,000 votes cast — a margin of about 12,600 votes.
key_facts.excerpt: Public broadcaster RUV reported that 52.8% of the more than 225,000 people who voted had rejected the government's proposal, while 47.2% had backed it. Some 12,600 votes separated them.

key_facts.fact: Turnout was 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009, out of some 270,000 eligible voters.
key_facts.excerpt: With some 270,000 people eligible to vote, RUV reported the turnout of 82.5% was the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009.

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir said the EU membership question would not be revisited while her government remains in power; her term runs to 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: She told a news conference on Sunday afternoon that the issue of EU membership would not be revisited while her government was in office.

key_facts.fact: Her centre-left government had promised a referendum by 2027 but brought it forward because of international tensions, including President Trump's threats against Greenland.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's centre-left government promised to hold a referendum by 2027, but brought it forward because of international tensions, including US President Donald Trump's threats against Greenland.

key_facts.fact: The result split urban and rural Iceland: both Reykjavík constituencies backed 'Yes' while fishing communities delivered 'No' majorities above 65% in several districts. Iceland's EEA and Schengen memberships are unaffected.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in Reykjavík North and Reykjavík South both backed "Yes" comfortably but that support evaporated outside the capital … Fishing communities where opposition to EU quota-sharing rules has run deep for over a decade, delivered "No" majorities above 65% in several districts. … the country already participates in the European Economic Area and the passport-free Schengen zone, and both arrangements stay intact.

stories.headline: Arrowhead's plozasiran cuts triglycerides ~80% and reduces pancreatitis in two Phase 3 trials

key_facts.fact: Arrowhead presented pivotal Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 results for plozasiran in severe hypertriglyceridemia on August 30 in a Hot Line Late-Breaking Science session at the ESC Congress 2026 in Munich.
key_facts.excerpt: PASADENA, Calif., August 30, 2026--Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today presented results from the pivotal Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 studies of plozasiran in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG) during a Hot Line Late-Breaking Science session at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress 2026 in Munich, Germany.

key_facts.fact: Both trials met their primary and all prespecified secondary endpoints, with median triglyceride reductions from baseline of 79% and 81% at Month 12 (p<0.0001 in both).
key_facts.excerpt: SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 met their primary and all prespecified secondary endpoints and demonstrated deep and durable reductions in triglycerides (TG), with median reductions from baseline of 79% and 81%, respectively at Month 12 (p<0.0001 in both studies).

key_facts.fact: A prespecified pooled analysis showed plozasiran significantly reduced acute pancreatitis events, with greater absolute benefit among patients at higher risk.
key_facts.excerpt: In a prespecified pooled analysis, plozasiran also significantly reduced acute pancreatitis (AP) events across the broad sHTG study population, with greater absolute benefit observed among patients at higher risk of AP.

key_facts.fact: More than 90% of plozasiran-treated patients in both studies reached triglyceride levels below 500 mg/dL at Month 12, and more than half fell below 150 mg/dL.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 90% of plozasiran-treated patients in both studies achieved TG levels below 500 mg/dL (<5.65 mmol/L) at Month 12, and more than half achieved TG levels below 150 mg/dL (<1.69 mmol/L).

key_facts.fact: Arrowhead plans to file a supplemental NDA with the FDA before the end of 2026 and to use an FDA Priority Review Voucher it purchased on August 4, 2026 to accelerate the review.
key_facts.excerpt: beginning with a planned supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) before the end of 2026. On August 4, 2026, the company announced it had purchased an FDA Priority Review Voucher, which it intends to utilize for this application.

sources.title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Presents Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 Data Demonstrating Plozasiran Reduced Acute Pancreatitis Events in Patients with Severe Hypertriglyceridemia
